title: Grunge Aesthetic & Flannel Shirts
summary: Anti-fashion movement originating in Seattle music culture, characterized by oversized plaid flannel shirts, distressed denim, Doc Martens boots, and layered thrift store clothes.
facts: Brought into high fashion by Marc Jacobs' spring 1993 Perry Ellis collection.
Rooted in practical Pacific Northwest outdoor wear adapted by indie musicians.
Symbolized 90s youth rebellion and apathy towards polished 80s glam.

title: JNCO Wide-Leg Jeans
summary: Ultra-wide denim trousers with leg openings measuring up to 50 inches, hugely popular among ravers, skaters, and nu-metal youth culture.
facts: Founded by brothers Jacques Revah and Haim Revah in Los Angeles (JNCO stands for 'Judge None Choose One').
Featured massive embroidered back pockets capable of holding entire hand-held consoles or spray paint cans.
Became an essential uniform of late-90s skateboarding and rave subcultures.

title: Neon Windbreakers & Tracksuits
summary: Vibrant, crinkled nylon windbreakers featuring bold geometric color-blocking in neon teal, magenta, purple, and gold.
facts: Widely worn across high school campuses, hip-hop music videos, and athletic events.
Utilized lightweight crinkle nylon and mesh lining.

title: Chunky Platform Shoes & Sneakers
summary: Towering platform sneakers and boots featuring 3 to 5 inch elevated soles, popularized by pop stars like the Spice Girls.
facts: Buffalo Boots of Germany manufactured the iconic 1310-2 model platforms.
Defined clubwear and pop star aesthetics in mid-to-late 90s Europe and America.
Influenced casual footwear designs across high street fashion brands.

title: Starter Snapback & Satin Jackets
summary: Pro sports team licensed snapback baseball caps and satin break-away jackets featuring embroidered team logos and the signature Starter 'S and Star' logo.
facts: Popularized by hip-hop groups like N.W.A, Run-DMC, and 90s athletes.
Featured adjustable plastic snap closures and silver satin inner lining.
High demand made them coveted fashion status symbols in urban youth culture.
